question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.
sql:
-- Final query: absolute difference between average customer spending
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        al.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS TotalSales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
    GROUP BY al.ArtistId, ar.Name
),
top_artist AS (
    SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY TotalSales DESC, ArtistName ASC LIMIT 1
),
low_artist AS (
    SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY TotalSales ASC, ArtistName ASC LIMIT 1
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        inv.CustomerId,
        al.ArtistId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_spending_on_artist
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
    WHERE al.ArtistId IN (
        (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist),
        (SELECT ArtistId FROM low_artist)
    )
    GROUP BY inv.CustomerId, al.ArtistId
),
avg_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        cs.ArtistId,
        AVG(cs.total_spending_on_artist) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending cs
    GROUP BY cs.ArtistId
)
SELECT ABS(
    (SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist)) -
    (SELECT avg_spending FROM avg_spending WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM low_artist))
) AS absolute_difference

How this database is organised (written by an LLM from the tables' notes and keys):
The main transactional tables are invoices and invoice_items, which record sales events. Invoices link to customers via CustomerId, while invoice_items connect invoices to specific tracks using InvoiceId and TrackId respectively. The tracks table serves as the central entity for media content, linking to albums, genres, and media types through AlbumId, GenreId, and MediaTypeId. These three—albums, genres, and media types—are lookup tables providing descriptive details for the tracks. Artists are linked to albums via ArtistId, and employees support customers via SupportRepId. Playlists and their contents are managed through the playlists and playlist_track table, with playlist_track acting as a junction table linking playlists to tracks.

function.name: run_sql_query
function.arguments:
{"sql": "-- Calculate average spending per customer for top-selling artist (Iron Maiden) and lowest-selling artist
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        al.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS TotalSales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
    GROUP BY al.ArtistId, ar.Name
),
top_artist AS (
    SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY TotalSales DESC, ArtistName ASC LIMIT 1
),
low_artist AS (
    SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY TotalSales ASC, ArtistName ASC LIMIT 1
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        ii.InvoiceId,
        t.AlbumId,
        al.ArtistId,
        inv.CustomerId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spending
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN invoices inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
    WHERE al.ArtistId IN (
        (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist),
        (SELECT ArtistId FROM low_artist)
    )
    GROUP BY ii.InvoiceId, t.AlbumId, al.ArtistId, inv.CustomerId
)
SELECT 
    cs.ArtistId,
    ar.Name AS ArtistName,
    cs.CustomerId,
